walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration $a(t) = 0.1 t^{3/2}$ with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \int 0.1 t^{3/2}\,dt = 0.1\left(\frac{t^{5/2}}{5/2}\right) + C = 0.04 t^{5/2} + C$$

Apply the initial condition $v(0) = 1.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$C = 1.72 \implies v(t) = 0.04 t^{5/2} + 1.72$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Integrates to obtain $v = 0.04 t^{5/2} + 1.72$, sets $v = 3$, and solves to find $t = 4\text{ s}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between acceleration and velocity:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$

Substitute the acceleration function $a(t) = 0.1 t^{3/2}$:
$$v(t) = \int 0.1 t^{3/2}\,dt$$
Use the power rule for integration:
$$v(t) = 0.1 \times \frac{t^{3/2 + 1}}{3/2 + 1} + C = 0.1 \times \frac{t^{5/2}}{5/2} + C$$
$$v(t) = 0.1 \times \frac{2}{5} t^{5/2} + C = 0.04 t^{5/2} + C$$

Find the constant $C$ using initial velocity $v(0) = 1.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$1.72 = 0.04(0) + C \implies C = 1.72$$
So the velocity function is:
$$v(t) = 0.04 t^{5/2} + 1.72$$

Find the time $t$ when the velocity equals $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$0.04 t^{5/2} + 1.72 = 3$$
Subtract $1.72$ from both sides:
$$0.04 t^{5/2} = 1.28$$
Divide by $0.04$:
$$t^{5/2} = \frac{1.28}{0.04} = 32$$
Raise both sides to the power $\frac{2}{5}$:
$$t = 32^{2/5} = (32^{1/5})^2 = 2^2 = 4\text{ s}$$
